column1: Manufacturing costing software - buyer’s checklist (from the Emithran buyer’s guide)

How to use: set a weight for each row (3 = must-have, 2 = important, 1 = nice to have) before any demos. Score each vendor 0-3 (0 = no, 1 = weak, 2 = adequate, 3 = strong) and record the evidence. Weighted score = weight x score.

column2: Question
Does it predict cost (should-cost), or only record it?
Bottom-up estimates with visible, editable assumptions?
Early-stage and detailed estimates in the same tool?
Calibration against our quotes and actuals?
Results from our own five test parts within an agreed tolerance?
Covers the processes behind our top 80% of spend?
Regional rates, kept current and open to our overrides?
Compares designs, materials, locations and volumes?
CAD, PLM, ERP and procurement connections: standard or custom?
Versioning, roles, approvals, audit trail?
SSO, data hosting and IT review passed?
Three-year total including services and growth?
Training, response times, named contacts?
Customers in our industry we can speak to?
What to do
Choose 5 to 20 representative parts covering the processes behind your top 80% of spend, each with a recent trusted quote or actual cost
Decide in advance what difference from the known cost counts as acceptable (e.g. within +/-10%)
Ask each vendor to build the estimates in a working session, using the same drawings and volumes
Capture cycle times, rates, scrap and overhead used, so differences can be explained
Measure the error per part and the average bias; then let each vendor calibrate and re-run
Combine the pilot result with the checklist score above
